newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico may slap tariffs on China footwear imports.
newsitem.headline: Mexico may slap tariffs on China footwear imports.

text.p: Mexico's Trade Ministry said Tuesday it intended to impose tariffs on Chinese footwear imports of between 165 and 1,105 percent.
The ministry said the move, to be announced Wednesday through the government's Official Gazette, was a preliminary resolution of the revision of an earlier definitive resolution.
The compensatory tariffs vary between the two percentage figures, according to the classification of the footwear entering the country, the ministry said.
The ministry said the tariffs would underscore the government's goal of clamping down on "disloyal practices in international trade".
That is Mexico's usual euphemism for "dumping" product at prices lower than production cost or prices lower than those prevailing in the country of origin.
The ministry said the move would continue to help stem the damage that imports bring to the national footwear industry. The domestic industry employs 180,000 people, it said.
